qualification_definitions.software_qualified: The exact source tree passed the repository's unit, integration, privileged-loop, native ARM64, package, and reproducibility gates. This does not establish physical firmware behavior.
qualification_definitions.physical_qualified: An immutable candidate has recorded PASS evidence for the stated hardware, firmware, Secure Boot state, source image, and USB. Results do not generalize beyond the recorded matrix.
qualification_definitions.full_upstream_parity: The Linux product matches the materially relevant behavior and breadth of the pinned Windows Rufus upstream feature. A bounded subset is not full parity.

status_definitions.implemented: An end-to-end Linux-native software path exists and is software-qualified for the stated scope. This status does not by itself imply full upstream breadth or physical qualification.
status_definitions.partial: A useful software-qualified subset exists, but upstream breadth, supported media, firmware behavior, or another material capability remains missing or unqualified.
status_definitions.in_progress: Implementation is active but is not yet an enabled and software-qualified end-to-end product path.
status_definitions.planned: Suitable for a Linux-native implementation but not yet present.
status_definitions.not_portable: Depends on a Windows-only provider or filesystem with no verified Linux equivalent.
status_definitions.deferred: Deliberately outside the current critical path and not promised for the next release.

features.upstream_feature: Create bootable drives from disk images, including compressed and virtual-disk images
features.notes: Raw, ISOHybrid, ZIP, gzip, bzip2, XZ, LZMA, Zstandard, VHD, VHDX, QCOW2, and VMDK inputs use source/target identity checks, cancellation, flush, and optional physical-device verification. Software qualification is complete for the stated formats; broad physical controller and flash-media coverage remains part of the hardware matrix rather than an upstream feature gap.

features.upstream_feature: Choose ISO Image mode or DD Image mode for ISOHybrid media
features.notes: Suitable ARM64 UEFI Linux optical media receive Rufus-style ISO Image mode, with DD retained only when a coherent raw MBR/GPT disk layout exists. Marker-bound inspection separates Windows installation media from Linux optical media: ISO9660 requires unique sources/boot.wim plus a supported install payload, while Microsoft UDF bridge media require bounded Microsoft/CDIMAGE descriptor provenance before the destructive Windows planner independently validates the mounted payload. ISO Image mode exposes Automatic, FAT32, or NTFS; Automatic prefers FAT32 and selects NTFS only when the complete inspected tree is FAT32-incompatible. Reviewed MBR/GPT, 4/8/16/32 KiB cluster, and filesystem-specific label choices are bound through confirmation, the privileged helper, diagnostics, result evidence, copied-file SHA-256 verification, filesystem checking, flushing, and detached readback. NTFS uses one data partition plus the exact pinned 1 MiB UEFI:NTFS boot image with shared Windows/Linux layout and metadata handling. A bounded versioned headless corpus binds Ubuntu 26.04 Desktop ARM64, signed-checksum Debian 13.6.0 ARM64 netinst, signed-checksum Fedora Everything 44 aarch64 netinst, signed-checksum openSUSE Tumbleweed AArch64 DVD media, and deterministic ISO-image, DD-only, and refusal fixtures. Physical write/readback passed on one Kingston USB-attached target for Ubuntu MBR/UEFI/NTFS, Debian GPT/UEFI/FAT32, and Fedora optical-only MBR/UEFI/FAT32 extraction. BIOS/CSM or dual-mode Linux extraction, NTFS persistence, distribution-specific adaptations, firmware boot, Secure Boot behavior, and a representative hardware matrix remain outside this bounded path. Additional distribution names are deferred unless they expose a distinct media-layout regression.

GPT/MBR, UEFI, x86 BIOS/CSM, FAT32, NTFS, WIM splitting, UEFI:NTFS, setup options, driver staging, SkuSiPolicy, qualified Windows UEFI CA 2023 replacement, and guarded UEFI/NTFS silent-install media are implemented through Linux-native tooling. Windows and Linux NTFS media share the pinned UEFI:NTFS geometry and metadata implementation. Silent installation binds exact WIM indexes and boot.wim language, refuses pre-existing answer files, requires a separate disk-0 acknowledgement, and uses the verified UEFI:NTFS partition as a fail-open disk-numbering guard. A separate experimental Windows To Go ARM64 backend now applies Windows directly to NTFS and constructs a GUID-bound ESP/BCD/SAN-policy layout. FAT32 silent-install parity, graphical Windows To Go selection, and broader physical Windows Setup/firmware coverage remain bounded gaps.

features.upstream_feature: Customize Windows Setup and OOBE behavior
features.notes: Hardware-check bypass, offline/local account, localized reserved-account-name rejection, privacy, regional settings, time zone, BitLocker suppression, driver loading, the Rufus 4.15 Quality of Life policy, installed-system SkuSiPolicy deployment, qualified Windows UEFI CA 2023 selection, and guarded UEFI/NTFS silent installation are implemented through deterministic XML, CLI, GTK, repeated media analysis, and exact readback contracts. Silent mode binds the selected WIM index and boot.wim language, refuses existing unattended files, requires all upstream prerequisites, appends a visible SILENT label, and adds an independent three-part disk-0 warning. The entry remains partial because FAT32 silent-install parity and physical Windows installation qualification are not claimed.

Guarded GPT/UEFI creation, verified writable-tree copy, identity-bound GUI flow, and checksum-backed reboot qualification are available for qualified Ubuntu casper and Debian live-boot media. Broader Rufus distribution coverage, including distribution-specific adaptations and a representative physical ARM64 matrix, remains missing; therefore this is a bounded subset rather than full implementation parity.

features.upstream_feature: Perform runtime validation of UEFI bootable media
features.notes: Descriptor-rooted UEFI structural and Secure Boot analysis, Rufus-compatible md5sum manifests, full-tree verification, a reproducibly built ARM64 validation loader, transactional installation, and QEMU chainload qualification are implemented. The optional loader is unsigned, Secure Boot acceptance is not established, and physical firmware qualification remains pending; those material boundaries prevent a full implementation-parity claim.

features.upstream_feature: Compute MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, and SHA-512 checksums
features.notes: All four Rufus-compatible image checksum algorithms are available in one descriptor-bound pass. MD5 and SHA-1 are explicitly excluded from trust decisions.

features.upstream_feature: Perform bad-block checks, including fake flash-drive detection
features.notes: The dedicated Linux-native qualification workflow provides quick two-pattern sampling and full four-pattern complete-capacity verification using address-derived data, synchronized writes, sentinel-first readback, alias-owner matching for wrapped/fake capacity, cancellation evidence, and deterministic passed/failed/cancelled reports. GTK exports reusable private no-replace JSON evidence bound to the reviewed device path and identity token. Broad physical-media coverage remains ordinary qualification scope rather than a missing software path.

features.upstream_feature: Create DD/VHD, VHDX, FFU, and ISO images of an existing drive
features.notes: Identity-bound raw, dynamic VHD, dynamic VHDX, and mounted-filesystem ISO/UDF backup are implemented through descriptor-only trusted providers, reviewed source binding/content evidence, content comparison, conservative destination admission, atomic no-replace publication, CLI/GTK integration, privileged loop qualification, native ARM64 execution, and reproducible Debian packaging. ISO/UDF capture remasters one mounted filesystem and does not claim whole-disk or bootable capture. FFU capture remains unimplemented.

An explicit experimental Windows 11 client ARM64 GPT/UEFI/NTFS path is implemented through Linux-native tooling. It binds the exact WIM image index, language, expanded size, source identity, target identity, capacity, and sector geometry before erasure; applies the selected image directly to unmounted NTFS with the reproducible package-owned WIM engine; creates a 260 MiB unlabelled FAT32 ESP; writes backup-first and readback-verifies GPT with the no-default-drive-letter attribute; derives BCD transactionally from Microsoft's applied BCD-Template with exact disk/ESP/OS GUID records and recovery disabled; installs ARM64 EFI fallback files; writes offline SAN policy 4; and independently remounts both filesystems read-only for hash, PE, BCD, policy, filesystem, and GPT verification. The production transaction passed on a 32 GiB loop disk using the real Microsoft Windows 11 25H2 ARM64 ISO and image 3. The status remains partial because Microsoft removed Windows To Go support, encrypted-file and extended-attribute restoration remain upstream wimlib limitations, the GUI surface and physical firmware/first-boot qualification are separate evidence, and no universal compatibility claim is made.

features.upstream_feature: Download official Microsoft Windows and UEFI Shell images
features.notes: Resumable verified acquisition, threshold-signed metadata, rollback-resistant cache, GUI workflow, and offline administration tools exist. Production offline-key ceremony and signed catalog publication remain pending.

The dedicated guarded non-bootable formatter implements FAT16, FAT32, exFAT, NTFS, UDF, ext2, ext3, and ext4 through MBR/GPT planning, trusted formatter resolution, filesystem-specific label and geometry checks, read-only post-format verification, and real loop qualification. FAT32, NTFS, and ext4 also serve applicable boot or persistence workflows. FAT32 retains conservative uppercase ASCII semantics; NTFS preserves exact valid Unicode and case through GUI, helper, physical format, and readback evidence. FAT16 uses an explicit below-4-GiB compatibility boundary and independent BPB cluster-count verification. UDF uses a fixed stable 2.01 hard-disk profile with exact block geometry, bounded OSTA Unicode labels, udfinfo/blkid agreement, closed-integrity evidence, and a private read-only kernel mount because Linux has no general UDF repair checker. ext2, ext3, and ext4 use distinct formatter contracts and independent ext-superblock feature classification so the requested generation cannot be blurred by generic ext-family probing. ReFS has no verified Linux-native formatter and is not portable today.

features.upstream_feature: Create FreeDOS or MS-DOS bootable drives
features.notes: Deterministic FreeDOS 1.4 media creation is complete. MS-DOS binary acquisition and licensing-dependent creation are not implemented.

features.upstream_feature: Read, write, and capture Full Flash Update images
features.notes: A Linux-native, explicitly experimental single-store-v1 full-flash restore path is implemented in CLI and GTK: bounded inspection and descriptor planning, source-chunk verification, catalog signature and explicit trust/publisher policies, exact reviewed-input and removable-target binding, exclusive acquisition, one-shot execution, synchronization, complete written-extent readback, cancellation evidence, and privileged loop qualification. Staged-GPT, partial-update, validation-descriptor, optimized/split, fixed/internal-disk, and unknown profiles remain refused; FFU capture is not implemented. Physical vendor-image restoration and firmware boot qualification remain pending and no production hardware-support claim is made. Upstream Rufus delegates FFU operations to Windows DISM/FfuProvider and does not supply a portable executor.

features.upstream_feature: Provide UEFI:NTFS boot support across firmware architectures
features.notes: Verified x86, x86-64, and ARM64 UEFI:NTFS assets are integrated. The exact pinned Rufus 4.15 image, including its Snapdragon X ARM64 correction, is shared by Windows installation and Linux NTFS ISO Image mode. Upstream Rufus 4.15 adds RISC-V64 support, which remains planned and is outside current ARM64 qualification.

features.upstream_feature: Extract limited El Torito UEFI images for firmware and nonstandard optical media
features.notes: A bounded Linux-native parser and read-only extractor validates El Torito descriptors and catalogs, selects one unambiguous EFI no-emulation image, preserves the pinned 8 MiB small-count compatibility rule, and binds deterministic source/catalog/image evidence. Automatic write-path selection, broader media-specific integration, and physical firmware qualification remain planned.

GTK strings and diagnostics must move into a translation catalog before language packs are accepted. Localized Windows account-name safety is implemented, but that does not constitute interface localization.

features.upstream_feature: Small portable executable and updateable distribution
features.notes: The Debian package is reproducible, executes natively on ARM64, includes privileged helpers, the WIM engine, and the complete FFU graphical dependency closure, and fails its build when any reachable project-local Python import is omitted. Threshold-signed release metadata, offline canonicalization/assembly/verification tooling, a read-only update decision, authenticated pinned-channel metadata refresh with verified offline cache fallback, exact package download, and owner-only persistent rollback state are implemented. The rollback transaction binds root and release metadata versions/digests, release-version monotonicity, and acceptance time under no-follow ownership checks, an exclusive lock, atomic replacement, synchronization, and clock-rollback refusal. Download reuses the bounded acquisition writer, and immutable root/release snapshots prevent post-verification field mutation. Canonical tagging now waits for a separately reviewed signed metadata tag, while staged and downloaded release directories are descriptor-bound and matched exactly to the authenticated asset inventory before upload and after publication. Production release keys and signed envelopes, package-manager installation/rollback, and AppImage or another audited portable format remain pending.

features.upstream_feature: Dark mode, tooltips, keyboard navigation, and accessible UI
features.notes: GTK keyboard navigation, assistive names, selectable diagnostics, resizable layout, and system-theme behavior exist. Complete option tooltips, explicit light/dark selection, and translation-aware accessibility review remain planned.
